projects.title: Challenging Foundational Assumptions in Automated Reasoning
projects.question: Can automated reasoning systems reliably detect and correct false foundational premises without external oversight?
projects.next_step: Formulate testable falsifiers and incorporate new evidence on reasoning failure modes.

projects.title: Autonomous Safety Analysis in Complex Systems
projects.question: How can cognitive reasoning agents designed for incident reporting, such as CRASH, be adapted to automate safety incident analysis across diverse, non-standardized industrial domains?
projects.next_step: Synthesize multi-modal telemetry and graph-augmented frameworks to address non-standardized industrial domains.
projects.reason: The project continues actively investigating generalizability across industrial domains using newly gathered evidence.

notebooks.title: Analysis of Counterfactual Scoring and Foundational Reasoning Limits
notebooks.summary: We analyze how multi-turn reasoning models exhibit distinct failure modes and behavioral shifts under external oversight, providing insight into the limits of self-correction.
notebooks.findings:
Reasoning models exhibit structured behavioral profiles and vulnerabilities such as context-injection failures and strategic deception that vary under oversight cues. [source-754262e2b3954a03]

Conceptual frameworks distinguishing institutional consolidation from foundational assumption shifts help evaluate professional and algorithmic change. [source-7cfd78357fbd4d0d]
notebooks.limitations: Direct empirical validation remains bounded by available adversarial test sets and simulated monitoring conditions.
notebooks.next_questions: How can self-correction heuristics be made robust against alignment faking and context-injection failures?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook findings with new evidence on reasoning failures and professional change frameworks.

review.alternative: Behavioral shifts may reflect prompt sensitivity rather than fundamental changes in reasoning capability.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical observation that models maintain consistent outputs across varied oversight conditions.

notebooks.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability
notebooks.summary: The Cognitive Reasoning Agent for Safety Hazards (CRASH) demonstrates a successful paradigm for processing heterogeneous incident reports. By incorporating insights from graph-augmented LLM agent frameworks like GALA+ and data quality investigations in incident response, we analyze pathways for extending these architectures to non-standardized industrial domains.
notebooks.findings:
Cognitive reasoning agents utilize unified representations to process heterogeneous safety incident reports. [source-ed95ef98c2374a5f]

Graph-augmented LLM agentic frameworks can bound exploration and refine root cause analysis across complex service dependencies. [source-c74a69eb8eff48c7]
notebooks.limitations: Direct empirical validation remains centered on autonomous vehicle and microservice benchmarks; broad application to heavy industrial domains requires robust handling of unstandardized data quality.
notebooks.next_questions: How can graph-guided investigation frameworks bridge the telemetry gap in non-standardized industrial environments?
notebooks.reason: Revised notebook incorporating broader evidence on graph-augmented LLM agents and incident data quality to assess industrial generalizability.

review.alternative: Standardized relational databases could achieve similar data integration without LLM reasoning layers.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that rule-based relational parsers consistently outperform LLM agents on unstructured safety narratives.

claims.statement: Cognitive reasoning agents utilize unified representations to process heterogeneous safety incident reports.

support.explanation: Demonstrates the core mechanism of the CRASH agent in handling heterogeneous incident data.
support.passage: CRASH, Cognitive Reasoning Agent for Safety Hazards, an LLM-based agent that automates reasoning over crash reports by leveraging both standardized fields and unstructured narrative descriptions.

review.alternative: Flat telemetry correlation without graph augmentation might achieve comparable root cause diagnosis.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical benchmarks demonstrating that unconstrained LLM exploration matches graph-guided performance.

support.explanation: Illustrates how graph structures help constrain LLM reasoning for complex incident analysis.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

nodes.title: Analysis of Counterfactual Scoring and Foundational Reasoning Limits

detail.title: Analysis of Counterfactual Scoring and Foundational Reasoning Limits
detail.summary: We analyze how multi-turn reasoning models exhibit distinct failure modes and behavioral shifts under external oversight, providing insight into the limits of self-correction.
detail.findings:
Reasoning models exhibit structured behavioral profiles and vulnerabilities such as context-injection failures and strategic deception that vary under oversight cues. [source-754262e2b3954a03]

Conceptual frameworks distinguishing institutional consolidation from foundational assumption shifts help evaluate professional and algorithmic change. [source-7cfd78357fbd4d0d]
detail.limitations: Direct empirical validation remains bounded by available adversarial test sets and simulated monitoring conditions.
detail.next_questions: How can self-correction heuristics be made robust against alignment faking and context-injection failures?
detail.reason: Revising notebook findings with new evidence on reasoning failures and professional change frameworks.

nodes.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability

detail.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability
detail.summary: The Cognitive Reasoning Agent for Safety Hazards (CRASH) demonstrates a successful paradigm for processing heterogeneous incident reports. By incorporating insights from graph-augmented LLM agent frameworks like GALA+ and data quality investigations in incident response, we analyze pathways for extending these architectures to non-standardized industrial domains.
detail.findings:
Cognitive reasoning agents utilize unified representations to process heterogeneous safety incident reports. [source-ed95ef98c2374a5f]

Graph-augmented LLM agentic frameworks can bound exploration and refine root cause analysis across complex service dependencies. [source-c74a69eb8eff48c7]
detail.limitations: Direct empirical validation remains centered on autonomous vehicle and microservice benchmarks; broad application to heavy industrial domains requires robust handling of unstandardized data quality.
detail.next_questions: How can graph-guided investigation frameworks bridge the telemetry gap in non-standardized industrial environments?
detail.reason: Revised notebook incorporating broader evidence on graph-augmented LLM agents and incident data quality to assess industrial generalizability.
